name: adb_android_basic
description: General Android UI operations over ADB: screen reading, Settings, launcher, Back, scrolling, quick-action contracts, cross-app navigation, and state recovery. Requires Settings, Clock, and a launcher with a swipe-up app drawer. Text-entry diagnostics are in adb_android_text_editing.

trace_observations.description: Agent loaded device-operator via skill_read before operating the phone UI (informational only).

tasks.prompt: Look at the current screen and tell me what is on it.
tasks.description_for_judge: The agent should call screenshot and describe the current Android screen.

rubric.description: The agent briefly described the screen contents.

tasks.description_for_judge: The agent should open system Settings (using quick_action open_settings or tapping the Settings icon). The final screenshot should show Settings.

rubric.description: The agent opened the Settings app.
The agent confirmed the Settings screen with a screenshot.

tasks.prompt: Open Settings, check whether Wi-Fi is currently enabled, and tell me its status.
tasks.description_for_judge: The agent should open Settings, navigate to Network & Internet (or WLAN/Internet), and correctly report whether Wi-Fi is currently enabled or disabled.

rubric.description: The agent found and viewed the Wi-Fi/network settings.
The agent correctly reported whether Wi-Fi was enabled or disabled.

tasks.prompt: From the Home screen, swipe up to open the app drawer. Leave the drawer visible and name two applications actually displayed. Do not open an app.
tasks.description_for_judge: From the Home screen, swipe up to open the app drawer. Leave the drawer visible and name two applications actually displayed. Do not open an app. Judge only the supplied pre/post screenshots and successful tool results. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The pre-screenshot shows the launcher Home screen.
A successful upward swipe is recorded and the post-screenshot shows the app drawer, rather than Home, search results, or another app.
The two applications named in the answer are visible in the post-screenshot.

tasks.description_for_judge: Agent must navigate back from a settings sub-page to the parent settings page.

setup.prompt: Open system Settings, navigate to a subpage with a Back button (such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or About phone), and leave that subpage open.

rubric.check: Post-screenshot shows the parent or top-level Settings page after leaving the settings sub-page visible in the pre-screenshot.

tasks.description_for_judge: Agent must perform a vertical scroll downward on the current page.

setup.prompt: Open system Settings and stay near the top of the main Settings list. Do not open an individual settings page.

rubric.check: Post-screenshot shows lower content from the same settings list than the pre-screenshot, consistent with one downward scroll.

tasks.description_for_judge: Scroll the current Settings list down until its bottom is reached. Stop when further scrolling reveals no additional entries, and leave the last entries visible. Do not change settings. Judge only the supplied pre/post screenshots and successful tool results. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

setup.prompt: Open system Settings and stay near the top of the main Settings list. Do not open an individual settings page.

tasks.prompt: Scroll the current Settings list down until its bottom is reached. Stop when further scrolling reveals no additional entries, and leave the last entries visible. Do not change settings.

rubric.check: The pre-screenshot shows the main Settings list near its top.
The trace contains successful scrolling of that list; any sufficient number of scrolls is valid.
The post-screenshot shows the recognizable last entries of the same Settings list, rather than the initial top or middle. Blank padding alone does not prove the bottom was reached.
The final reply says the bottom was reached or no additional entries appeared.

tasks.description_for_judge: Use quick_action with action=home to return from Settings to Home. Leave Home visible. Judge only the supplied pre/post screenshots and successful tool results. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

setup.prompt: Open the main Settings page and leave it visible without a panel or dialog.

tasks.prompt: Use quick_action with action=home to return from Settings to Home. Leave Home visible.

rubric.check: The pre-screenshot shows Settings.
The post-screenshot shows the launcher Home screen, not Settings, recents, or a system panel.

tasks.description_for_judge: Use quick_action with action=app_switch to open recent apps. Leave recent apps open with the Settings card visible. Do not dismiss any app cards. Judge only the supplied pre/post screenshots and successful tool results. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

setup.prompt: Open the main Settings page and leave it visible without a panel or dialog.

tasks.prompt: Use quick_action with action=app_switch to open recent apps. Leave recent apps open with the Settings card visible. Do not dismiss any app cards.

rubric.check: The pre-screenshot shows Settings.
The post-screenshot shows recent apps with a recognizable Settings card visible; Home or a running app is insufficient.

tasks.description_for_judge: Use quick_action with action=notification_center to open notifications. Describe the visible notifications, or explicitly report that there are none. Leave the notification panel open and do not clear notifications. Judge only the supplied pre/post screenshots and successful tool results. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

setup.prompt: Return to the launcher Home screen and dismiss any notification or quick-settings panel.

tasks.prompt: Use quick_action with action=notification_center to open notifications. Describe the visible notifications, or explicitly report that there are none. Leave the notification panel open and do not clear notifications.

rubric.check: The pre-screenshot shows Home without the notification panel.
The post-screenshot shows the notification panel.
The answer accurately describes notifications visible in the post-screenshot or its visible empty state; do not credit claims about unseen notifications.

tasks.prompt: From Settings, open Clock and show its alarm list. Tell me how many alarms are displayed and leave the list visible. Do not change alarms.
tasks.description_for_judge: From Settings, open Clock and show its alarm list. Tell me how many alarms are displayed and leave the list visible. Do not change alarms. Judge only the supplied pre/post screenshots and successful tool results. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The pre-screenshot shows the main Settings page.
The post-screenshot shows the Clock alarm list, including its empty state if applicable.
The answer correctly reports the alarms displayed in the post-screenshot without claiming a total for unseen entries.

setup.prompt: Open the main Settings page and leave it visible without changing settings.

tasks.prompt: Read the notifications in the currently open panel and tell me what is visible, or that there are none. Close the panel to return to the main Settings page. Do not clear notifications.
tasks.description_for_judge: Read the notifications in the currently open panel and tell me what is visible, or that there are none. Close the panel to return to the main Settings page. Do not clear notifications. Judge only the supplied pre/post screenshots and successful tool results. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The pre-screenshot shows the notification panel.
The answer accurately describes notifications visible in the pre-screenshot, or its visible empty state. Do not credit unsupported claims.
The post-screenshot shows the main Settings page with the notification panel dismissed.

setup.prompt: Open the main Settings page, then open the notification panel over it. Leave the notification panel open without clearing notifications.

tasks.prompt: Read the device model on the current device-information page, then return one level to its parent Settings page. Tell me the model you observed, or explicitly say if the page did not show a model. Do not modify settings.
tasks.description_for_judge: Read the device model on the current device-information page, then return one level to its parent Settings page. Tell me the model you observed, or explicitly say if the page did not show a model. Do not modify settings. Judge only the supplied pre/post screenshots and successful tool results. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The pre-screenshot shows the device-information page; a different starting page does not satisfy the precondition.
The post-screenshot shows the parent Settings page, not Home or the initial device-information page.
The answer matches the model visible in the pre-screenshot, or correctly says none was shown when that screenshot contains no model.

setup.prompt: Open Settings and navigate to About phone or the equivalent device-information page. Make the device model visible if the page lists one. Leave this page open without changing settings.

tasks.prompt: Open the main Settings list and go to its top. Note two visible setting names. Scroll down until different entries are visible and observe them, then return to the top. Tell me the two names you first noted and leave them visible. Do not change settings.
tasks.description_for_judge: Open the main Settings list and go to its top. Note two visible setting names. Scroll down until different entries are visible and observe them, then return to the top. Tell me the two names you first noted and leave them visible. Do not change settings. Evaluate the observed UI and tool trace, not the final claim alone. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The trace shows a downward list exploration followed by screen observation and navigation back to the top; a final success claim alone is insufficient.
The final screenshot shows the top of the main Settings list.
The two names reported in the answer are visible in the final screenshot; localized names are accepted.

tasks.prompt: Return to Home, then reopen Settings. Tell me which page Settings actually reopened on and leave it visible. Do not change settings.
tasks.description_for_judge: Return to Home, then reopen Settings. Tell me which page Settings actually reopened on and leave it visible. Do not change settings. Judge only the supplied pre/post screenshots and successful tool results. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The pre-screenshot shows the device-information page in Settings.
Successful tool results record returning Home and subsequently opening Settings; an unsuccessful attempt alone is insufficient.
The post-screenshot shows Settings without an overlay, and the answer identifies that visible page. Either the main page or a restored subpage is valid.

setup.prompt: Open Settings and navigate to About phone or equivalent device information. Leave that page visible without changing settings.

tasks.prompt: Open the main Settings page, then open Clock. Use the recent-apps screen to return to Settings. Leave Settings visible; do not dismiss app cards.
tasks.description_for_judge: Open the main Settings page, then open Clock. Use the recent-apps screen to return to Settings. Leave Settings visible; do not dismiss app cards. Evaluate the observed UI and tool trace, not the final claim alone. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The trace shows Settings opened before Clock.
The trace shows the recent-apps screen being opened, observed, and used to select Settings. Simply opening Settings again from Home does not satisfy this task.
The final screenshot shows Settings without the recent-apps overlay.
